result: Coeliac disease is an inflammatory disorder of genetically predisposed persons triggered by an immune response to gluten, proteins of wheat, barley and rye. 90% to 95% of patients carry HLA-DQ2.5 (DQA1*05 and DQB1*02, in cis or trans); the remaining 5% to 10% carry HLA-DQ8 (DQA1*03 and DQB1*03:02) or HLA-DQ2.2; HLA risk alleles are necessary but not sufficient and confer about 35% to 40% of the genetic risk. Prevalence in western countries is about 0.7% histologically confirmed and 1% to 1.6% by serological screening. Recommendations: IgA anti-TG2 as the single initial test at any age, with total IgA, on a gluten-containing diet (moderate certainty, strong, 95% agreement); diagnosis without biopsy in adults when IgA anti-TG2 is at least 10 times the upper limit of normal (moderate certainty, conditional, 95%), confirmed in a second blood sample and, until more safety data are available, limited to patients under 45 years; HLA testing has a poor positive and a high negative predictive value, so HLA-DQ2/8 typing is not used routinely in initial diagnosis (moderate certainty, strong, 100%).
